battle.name: 八王之亂
battle.brief: 西晉元康元年（291）至永嘉元年（306），宗室諸王以「清君側」爭奪洛陽，十五年間執政者更迭，晉惠帝被挾持而遷徙。卡面的希臘重步兵屬公元前五世紀裝備，不在此役現場；晉軍沿用漢末三國之制，以大盾長槊結陣、弩弓齊射，最終決定洛陽與鄴城歸屬的，是匈奴、羯族騎兵與諸王自募的部曲。

kit.name: 希臘重步兵
kit.history: 方陣的重心不是個人，是互相遮蔽。盾牌接在一起時，一支軍隊的正面比一個人結實。

countries: 這場戰爭是西晉建立後第一次大規模內戰，自元康元年（291）至太安二年（306），前後十五年。交戰的兩邊並非兩個國家，而是同一王朝內部的宗室諸王、各方鎮將軍與被徵發的羌胡騎兵，爭奪的核心是洛陽城與晉惠帝司馬衷本人。名為「八王」者是汝南王司馬亮、楚王司馬瑋、趙王司馬倫、齊王司馬冏、長沙王司馬乂、成都王司馬穎、河間王司馬頴、東海王司馬越。制度上的根子埋於晉武帝分封同姓王二十七人：各王在封國置有屬官、領有武裝，州郡刺史又長期兼領方鎮兵權，宗室私兵與州郡精兵互相重疊，中央一旦失去秩序，兵符就變成可以互相追殺的憑據。開端是外戚太傅楊駿專權，元康元年六月司馬亮與司馬瑋廢駿，賈南風隨即借司馬瑋之手除掉亮，同年十一月再毒死司馬瑋。中段司馬倫弒惠帝自立僅得三個月，司馬冏、司馬乂、司馬穎、司馬頴聯軍討之；末段東海王司馬越起兵鄴城，天下兵柄歸於一系。與此同時三股外來武力在邊地舉兵：匈奴屠各部劉淵於太安元年（304）在離石左國城建國稱漢王，羯人石勒、氐人李雄、荊州張昌、關中趙廞各據一方，分散中央的注意力。最後介入戰局的第三方是前趙的劉聰與劉曜，311年洛陽陷落，八王之亂由宮廷內鬥演成兩晉斷裂。
countriesEn: This war was the first large-scale civil war of the Western Jin, running from Yuankang 1 (291) to Tai'an 2 (306) — fifteen years in all. The two sides were not two states but competing elements inside a single dynasty: princes of the imperial clan, regional commanders holding circuit authority, and levied Xianbei, Xiongnu and Di cavalry. What they fought over was the city of Luoyang and the person of Emperor Hui of Jin, Sima Zhong. The eight who gave the conflict its name were Prince Runan Sima Liang, Prince Chu Sima Wei, Prince Zhao Sima Lun, Prince Qi Sima Jiong, Prince Changsha Sima Ai, Prince Chengdu Sima Ying, Prince Hejian Sima Yong and Prince Donghai Sima Yue. The institutional root lay in Emperor Wu of Jin's enfeoffment of twenty-seven imperial kinsmen as kings: each prince had his own officials and armed following in his fief, while provincial governors long combined civil office with command of regional troops, so that princely retainers and provincial soldiers overlapped. Once the centre lost order, an army tally became a warrant to kill one's rivals. The opening move came with the regent Yang Jun, the empress's brother, monopolising power; in the sixth month of Yuankang 1, Sima Liang and Sima Wei deposed Yang Jun, and the empress Dowager Jia Nanfeng promptly used Sima Wei to remove Liang, then poisoned Wei himself in the eleventh month. In the middle phase Sima Lun murdered the emperor and reigned as emperor for only three months before a coalition of Sima Jiong, Sima Ai, Sima Ying and Sima Yong moved against him; in the final phase Prince Donghai Sima Yue rose at Ye and the empire's command of troops came into one pair of hands. At the same time three outside powers rose in the borderlands: the Xiongnu chieftain Liu Yuan founded the state of Han at Zuoguo city in Lishi in Tai'an 1 (304), the Jie chieftain Shi Le, the Di chieftain Li Xiong, the Jingzhou rebel Zhang Chang and the Guanzhong separatist Zhao Yin each held ground of their own, all of them pulling the centre's attention in different directions. The third party that eventually entered the war was Former Zhao under Liu Cong and Liu Yao, whose troops took Luoyang in 311, transforming a palace struggle into the fracture of the two Jin.
people: 關鍵人物分三層。第一層是被挾持的皇帝：晉惠帝司馬衷在位十餘年，幾乎每一場政變都以他的詔書為名，他本人卻從未真正決定任何一件事；太安元年成都王司馬穎被立為皇太弟後一度代行朝政，太安二年更被東海王司馬越以進餅的方式毒殺於洛陽。第二層是推動政變的宮廷人物：中宮賈南風在291年毒死司馬亮、廢黜司馬瑋，又在永康元年（300）毒殺太子司馬遹，逼出司馬倫與司馬冏的清算，最後自已在這場清算中被殺；吏部尚書張華依附中宮而掌機要，302年被司馬倫逼令自殺；太傅楊駿與外戚楊氏是291年第一場政變的目標。第三層是八王各自的結局：司馬亮、司馬瑋相繼被誅，司馬倫廢惠帝自立三個月後被迫自盡，司馬冏被司馬乂與司馬穎合謀刺殺，司馬乂在洛陽城破後被囚禁而遇害，司馬穎兵敗後流亡匈奴劉淵帳下終被殺，司馬頴退守河間兵敗被斬，司馬越雖是最後的勝者卻在病中死去，留下的是崩解的軍隊與空虛的朝廷。第四層是趁亂另立局面的人：匈奴屠各部劉淵自稱漢王，其子劉聰稱帝後派劉曜攻破洛陽；羯人石勒從劉淵部將轉為獨強，終建後趙；氐人李雄據成都建立成漢；荊州張昌、關中趙廞各以「天討」為名響應。而試圖收拾局面的人物則是並州刺史劉琨死守晉陽、豫州刺史祖逖在亂後北伐、以及以清談名士身份出任太傅、終至束手無策的王衍。
peopleEn: The key figures fall into four layers. The first is the emperor who was used: Emperor Hui of Jin, Sima Zhong, reigned for more than a decade, and almost every coup invoked his edicts, yet he never actually decided a single thing himself. In Tai'an 1, when Prince Chengdu Sima Ying was made heir apparent, he briefly exercised the powers of the court; in Tai'an 2 he was killed by poison in Luoyang, administered in a cake by Prince Donghai Sima Yue. The second layer is the palace figures who drove the coups: the empress Jia Nanfeng poisoned Sima Liang in 291 and put Sima Wei to death, then in Yongkang 1 (300) poisoned the crown prince Sima Yu, which forced the reckoning of Sima Lun and Sima Jiong, and she herself died in that reckoning. The Director of the Ministry of Personnel Zhang Hua rose by attaching himself to the empress and held the secretariat; in 302 Sima Lun forced him to kill himself. The Grand Tutor Yang Jun and the Yang clan were the target of the very first coup in 291. The third layer is the fate of the eight princes themselves: Sima Liang and Sima Wei were executed in turn; Sima Lun, having deposed the emperor and ruled for three months, was forced to take his own life; Sima Jiong was assassinated by a plot between Sima Ai and Sima Ying; Sima Ai was taken prisoner when Luoyang fell and met his death in custody; Sima Ying was routed and fled to the camp of the Xiongnu Liu Yuan, where he was killed; Sima Yong fell back to Hejian, was defeated and beheaded; and Sima Yue, the last victor, died of illness, leaving behind a disintegrating army and an empty court. The fourth layer is the men who built new orders out of the collapse: the Xiongnu chieftain Liu Yuan, who proclaimed himself King of Han, and his son Liu Cong, who became emperor and sent Liu Yao to take Luoyang; the Jie man Shi Le, who turned from a subordinate of Liu Yuan into an independent warlord and eventually founded Later Zhao; the Di man Li Xiong, who took Chengdu and built Cheng-Han; and Zhang Chang in Jingzhou and Zhao Yin in Guanzhong, who rose in the name of punishing the guilty. Those who tried to repair the situation were Liu Kun, Inspector of Bingzhou, holding Taiyuan against the Xiongnu, Zhu Ti, Inspector of Yuzhou, leading his northern expedition after the war, and Wang Yan, the talker-poet who became Grand Tutor and who ended with nothing to do.
kits: 卡面這件希臘重步兵屬公元前五世紀的城邦公民兵裝備，方陣由一人高的圓盾、青銅頭盔、胸甲與短矛組成，並未出現在三世紀末的洛陽戰場，這一點必須先說清楚：八王之亂的參戰者沒有任何一支部隊使用希臘式全套重步兵裝備。但它的戰術原理並不陌生——同樣的「互相遮蔽」思想，在漢末三國以來的中國軍隊裡以另一種物質形式延續了下來。晉軍的步兵骨架是「持大盾、列長槊」的密集步行陣：大盾多為橢圓形，漆木為胎、竹木為裡，外蒙牛皮或麻布，考古出土的東吳與曹魏漆木盾高逾一米、面寬約八十至九十公分，恰好可以遮住持盾者的身幹；長槊與戟沿用漢代形制，配環首刀作近身格鬥，鎧甲則以札甲、兩當甲為主，頭戴兜鍪，頸胸加護心鏡。弓弩方面，晉軍有張弓弩與蹶張弩，攻城則用投石機（飛石）、撞車、雲梯、巢車與地道，這一整套攻城技術是曹魏與孫吳在漢末留下的，未因八王之亂而消失。真正與希臘方陣形成尖銳對照的是兩點：其一，希臘方陣幾乎沒有騎兵，決定戰役的是正面厚度與公民兵的紀律；八王之亂中決定洛陽與鄴城歸屬的卻是匈奴、羯族與鮮卑騎兵，司馬穎、司馬頴聯軍與司馬越聯軍在河北平原上的衝撞，關鍵是馬腿而非盾牌。其二，希臘城邦的公民兵是一支自備裝備、為城邦而戰的集體，與皇帝之間有誓約；西晉的兵則是中央禁兵、州郡精兵與諸王募兵拼湊而成的臨時聯盟，一旦主將死亡或糧道斷絕，陣形就會在當夜解體——這正是八王之亂每一場戰役的共同結局。
kitsEn: The hoplite on the card belongs to the fifth century BC, the equipment of the citizen soldier of the Greek city-states: a round shield a man high, a bronze helmet, a cuirass and a short spear. It did not appear on the battlefield of Luoyang in the late third century AD, and that has to be stated plainly: not one of the formations that fought in the War of the Eight Princes used the full Greek heavy-infantry panoply. Yet the tactical principle is not alien — the same idea of mutual cover survived in China, in a different material form, in the armies that inherited the late Han and Three Kingdoms. The backbone of Jin infantry was a dense close-order line of large shields and long spears. The great shields were elliptical, built of lacquered wood with a bamboo-and-timber core, covered in hide or hemp cloth; the lacquered timber shields excavated from Eastern Wu and Cao Wei burials stand a little over a metre high and eighty to ninety centimetres across, just wide enough to cover the shield-bearer's trunk. Long spears and halberds kept their Han forms, ring-pommel sabres served for close combat, armour was mainly lamellar and two-piece cuirass, with iron helmets, neck and chest guards, and crossbows of the screw-and-tension types existed alongside the composite bow. For siege work the Jin used traction trebuchets, battering rams, scaling ladders, observation towers and mines — the whole technical inheritance of Cao Wei and Sun Wu, undamaged by the civil war. Two sharp contrasts with the Greek phalanx remain. First, the phalanx had almost no cavalry: battles were decided by the thickness of the front and the discipline of the citizen levy. In the War of the Eight Princes, by contrast, what decided Luoyang and Ye was the cavalry of the Xiongnu, Jie and Xianbei; the collisions of Sima Ying and Sima Yong's coalition with Sima Yue's on the North China plain were decided by horseflesh, not by shields. Second, the Greek citizen was a man who equipped himself and fought for his polis under oath. The Jin soldier was a patchwork of imperial guards, provincial picked troops and the levies of the princes; once a commander died or the supply line broke, the line came apart that same night — the common end of every engagement in this war.
tactics: 八王之亂的戰術，最大特點是「目標不在戰場而在宮廷」。每一方的軍事行動都必須以一份以晉惠帝名義發出的詔書為前提，於是奪取洛陽城、奪取惠帝本人、奪取發出詔書的能力，成了比攻城本身更迫切的目標。惠帝在十五年間被反覆遷徙：先後在洛陽、鄴城之間被迎來迎去，304年司馬穎兵敗後他甚至被帶到鄴城，作為司馬越討伐司馬穎的旗幟。洛陽城牆周約十三里，內有宮城，十二街貫通，防守方以弓弩、檑木、拒馬與出城反擊消耗進攻方；進攻方則以撞車撞擊城門與城牆、以雲梯附城、以飛石壓制城頭，並用地道與壕塹作業削弱基礎，攻城全靠器械與士氣硬磨。反攻的關鍵是內應：302年河間王司馬頴部將石超率兵五萬屯於洛陽城西，閉城拒守數月，長沙王司馬乂的守軍始終不能出城，終因城中人心崩潰而覆亡。前線的陣形則是典型的魏晉步兵樣式：弩手在前或兩翼齊射，槊兵結陣緩進，大盾兵遮蔽身幹，最後由環首刀兵貼身；騎兵在兩翼待機，衝破步陣裂縫後立刻轉為追擊與斷糧。兵眾方面，司馬穎與司馬頴聯軍及司馬越聯軍皆號稱十餘萬，但大量是裹挾的郡縣民兵與臨時徵發者，戰鬥力與名額相差懸殊。八陣圖一類的成條戰法仍為將領所熟悉，曹操所頒的戰法在曹魏將門中代代相傳，成為守城布陣的依據，但真正決定勝負的往往不是陣法而是後勤：洛陽糧食仰賴河北、山東沿黃河轉運，一旦運道被騎兵切斷，城中先飢餓而後崩潰。
tacticsEn: The defining tactic of the War of the Eight Princes was that the objective lay in the palace, not on the field. Every operation had to be premised on an edict issued in the name of Emperor Hui, so the capture of the city of Luoyang, the capture of the emperor himself, and the capture of the power to issue edicts all became more urgent than any ordinary siege. The emperor was shifted back and forth for fifteen years, ferried between Luoyang and Ye; after Sima Ying was routed in 304, he was even brought to Ye to serve as the banner of Sima Yue's campaign. The circuit of Luoyang's walls was about thirteen li, enclosing the palace city, with twelve streets running through it. The defenders answered with bows and crossbows, dropped beams, cheval-de-frise and sorties; the attackers brought rams against the gates, scaling ladders against the curtain, stone-throwers against the parapets, and undermined the foundations with mines and ditches, so that siege was a grinding business of machines and morale. The counter-stroke depended on the defence collapsing from within: in 302 the general Shi Cong of Prince Hejian Sima Yong brought fifty thousand men to the west of Luoyang and shut the city out for months, and the troops of Prince Changsha Sima Ai could never sortie; the city finally fell because its garrison lost heart. On the field the line was the standard Wei-Jin infantry pattern: crossbowmen opened with volleys from the front or the flanks, spearmen advanced in close order behind large shields, sabre-men closed at last; cavalry waited on both wings, and once it broke a gap in the foot it turned at once into pursuit and cutting of supplies. On numbers, the coalitions of Sima Ying and Sima Yong and of Sima Yue each claimed a hundred thousand men and more, but a large share were pressed locals and hastily summoned militiamen whose fighting quality bore no relation to their nominal strength. Formations codified in the old Eight Array Diagrams were still familiar to commanders, and the battle methods promulgated by Cao Cao had been handed down through the families of Cao Wei officers, serving as the basis of defensive deployment; yet what decided most engagements was not formation but supply. Luoyang drew its grain from Hebei and Shandong along the Yellow River, and once the convoy road was cut by cavalry, the city starved before it broke.
data: 時間與人口：《晉書·地理志》所載太康元年（280）西晉官方統計為戶二百四十五萬餘、口一千六百一十六萬餘，這是八王之亂前最後一次完整的人口普查，十五年戰亂後的數字已無可比對。戰役跨度為元康元年（291）至太安二年（306），計十五年，其間執掌洛陽的先後有中宮賈氏、司馬冏、司馬倫、司馬乂、司馬穎與司馬頴、司馬越等數方，宮廷政變以十數起計，時間短者只隔數月。城池與駐軍：洛陽城周約十三里，約合五點四公里，城內有宮城與十二街；中央禁兵分中軍宿衛與殿中宿衛，另有北軍五校尉分屯城內，兵額都在數千量級，地方州郡則各領精兵數千不等，一旦諸王舉兵，禁兵既無力分兵拒敵，也難以與方鎮兵力抗衡。兵眾規模：302年司馬穎與司馬頴聯軍自鄴、幽州南下，304年司馬越聯軍迎戰，兩軍皆以十餘萬為號，但史書所記真正投入戰鬥的，多為各州郡臨時徵發的民兵與郡兵。時間與結局：太安二年（306）六月晉惠帝遇毒崩於洛陽，七月司馬越病卒於鄴；304年劉淵在離石左國城稱漢王；308年劉聰稱帝並遣劉曜攻洛陽，晉軍大敗，屍骸遍野；311年六月洛陽陷落，懷帝被俘，宮室焚燒，史載死者以萬計；313年愍帝即位於長安，316年長安亦陷。
dataEn: Time and population: the official figures for the Western Jin in the first year of Taikang (280) recorded in the Geography Book of the Jin History are 2.45 million households and 16.16 million persons; this was the last complete census before the War of the Eight Princes, and no comparable figure survives for the aftermath of fifteen years of war. The war ran from Yuankang 1 (291) to Tai'an 2 (306), fifteen years in all, during which the holders of Luoyang in turn included the empress's party, Sima Jiong, Sima Lun, Sima Ai, Sima Ying with Sima Yong, and Sima Yue — six or more hands, and a palace coup every few months at the tightest. Cities and garrisons: the circuit of Luoyang's walls was about thirteen li, roughly 5.4 kilometres, enclosing the palace city and its twelve streets. The central garrison was divided between the middle army guarding the imperial palace and the palace troops, with the Northern Army's five colonels quartered inside the city; the strength of each was on the order of a few thousand, while the provinces each maintained picked troops numbering in the thousands. Once the princes rose, the palace guards were too few both to hold the city against them and to match the regional armies. Scale of the armies: in 302 the coalition of Sima Ying and Sima Yong moved south from Ye and Youzhou, and in 304 Sima Yue's coalition met them; both sides claimed a hundred thousand men and more, but what the histories actually put into the line was mostly militia hastily summoned from the prefectures and counties. Timing and outcome: in the sixth month of Tai'an 2 (306) Emperor Hui was poisoned and died at Luoyang; in the seventh month Sima Yue died of illness at Ye. In 304 Liu Yuan proclaimed himself King of Han at Zuoguo city in Lishi. In 308 Liu Cong assumed the imperial title and sent Liu Yao against Luoyang, where the Jin army was routed and the field was left thick with the dead; in the sixth month of 311 Luoyang fell, the emperor of Huai was taken captive, the palaces burned, and the histories put the dead in the tens of thousands. The emperor of Min was enthroned at Chang'an in 313, and Chang'an fell in 316.
cause: 八王之亂的起因，必須回到晉武帝晚年的政治安排。第一，太康元年分封同姓王二十七人，王國置有官屬、領有封土與武裝，而州郡刺史同時握有方鎮兵權，宗室與州郡各握一支可以獨立的武力，這在開國時是分封與郡縣並存的權宜之計，在第二代之後卻成了雙重威脅：中央要靠諸王出兵，諸王則據兵以自重。第二，滅吳之後朝廷曾裁撤州郡兵與屯田，宿衛與地方武力一併削弱，等到中央需要兵時，只能倚賴諸王與外戚的私兵，這使每一次宮廷鬥爭都必須以兵戎解決。第三，晉武帝立惠帝司馬衷為嗣，而惠帝無才無德，於是外戚楊駿與中宮賈南風輪流主持朝政；惠帝的太子司馬遹在永康元年被中宮毒殺，皇位繼承斷了血脈，正當性隨之崩塌，宗室便以「為太子報仇」為名起兵。第四，士族清談之風盛行，軍政人才斷層，中宮所用者如張華、裴頷雖有才而無兵，掌兵者則多為武人與外戚，權力與武力長期脫節。第五，五胡內徙已歷數十年，匈奴、羯、鮮卑、氐、羌的內附部眾住在塞內，為帝國充當騎兵與客兵；一旦中原內亂，這些武裝就成為各方爭取的資源，劉淵、石勒正是以這樣的部眾起家，劉淵並援引匈奴與漢室結為兄弟的舊說，自稱漢室外甥，以此為「漢王」的名分張目。
causeEn: The causes of the War of the Eight Princes must be traced back to the political arrangements of the last years of Emperor Wu of Jin. First, in the first year of Taikang he enfeoffed twenty-seven imperial kinsmen as kings; the princely fiefs had their own officials, their own lands and their own armed followers, while the provincial inspectors held command of regional troops. Holding a fief and holding a provincial command was a workable expedient when the empire was first founded and both a royal domain system and a commandery system ran side by side, but from the second generation onward it became a double threat: the centre had to rely on the princes for soldiers, and the princes used their soldiers to make themselves independent. Second, after the conquest of Wu the court curtailed the provincial armies and the tuntian, weakening both the guards and the local levies; whenever the centre needed troops again it had to turn to the private forces of princes and consort clans, so that every palace struggle had to be settled with arms. Third, Emperor Wu made the incapable Sima Zhong his heir; with no talent and no firmness, the regency passed in turn to the maternal clan of Yang and to the empress Jia Nanfeng. In Yongkang 1 the empress poisoned the crown prince Sima Yu, severing the succession line of the throne, and with it the legitimacy of the dynasty; the princes then rose under the banner of avenging the crown prince. Fourth, the fashion for lofty talk had hollowed out the officer corps; men such as Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who handled statecraft under the empress had no soldiers of their own, while those who held troops were military men and consort kinsmen, so that authority and armed force were permanently separated. Fifth, the Xiongnu, Jie, Xianbei, Di and Qiang had been settled inside the frontier for decades and served the empire as cavalry and as clients; once the interior broke down, that armed manpower became a resource every faction competed for. Liu Yuan and Shi Le rose on the strength of exactly such groups, and Liu Yuan invoked the old bond between the Xiongnu and the Han, styled himself a nephew of the Han house, and used that claim to make his title of King of Han intelligible.
impact: 八王之亂的直接後果是西晉的崩解，其長遠影響則改變了中國此後數百年的政治地理。第一，帝國的權力中心被徹底摧毀。洛陽兩度易主、兩度淪陷，宮室焚燒，府庫空虛；永嘉五年（311）洛陽陷落，懷帝被俘，愍帝僅以關中殘局苟延，316年長安亦為前趙所據，北方政權斷續數十年。第二，衣冠南渡。士族與中原人口沿江而下，琅邪王司馬睿在建康即位，東晉建立；北方門閥失去根基，江左門閥則在移民、莊園與武裝中重新壯大，「永嘉之亂，衣冠南渡」成為此後千年的文化分野。第三，內附的匈奴、羯、鮮卑、氐、羌趁亂建立割據政權：前趙（漢趙）、成漢先後於304年建國，後趙、前燕、前秦等接踵而至，北方進入十六國時代，戰亂延續近三百年，族群關係由融合轉為劇烈衝突。第四，制度上，軍隊地方化與方鎮化成為常態，方面統帥掌兵、州郡自募精兵的做法定型，而中正制與門閥在動盪中反而鞏固，成為隋唐選官制度的源頭。第五，佛教與胡文化在亂世中深入中原：洛陽淪陷前後佛圖澄等僧侶北上，後趙石勒對之禮敬，佛寺與胡風並肩進入北方城邑。第六，兵學與戰爭觀念的轉變：騎兵第一次在中國以壓倒性規模決定中原政治局勢，「以騎制步」成為後世北方政權的基本軍事前提。
impactEn: The direct consequence of the War of the Eight Princes was the disintegration of the Western Jin; its long-term effects reshaped the political geography of China for centuries. First, the power centre of the empire was destroyed. Luoyang changed hands twice and fell twice, the palaces burned and the treasuries emptied; in Yongjia 5 (311) Luoyang was taken, the emperor of Huai was captured, and the emperor of Min could hold out only on the remnant of Guanzhong until Chang'an too was taken by Former Zhao in 316, leaving northern government discontinuous for decades. Second, the great southward migration of the gentry. Clans and people from the north moved down the river; the Prince of Langya, Sima Rui, took the throne at Jiankang and the Eastern Jin was founded. The northern aristocracy lost its base, while the clans of the lower Yangtze grew strong on refugees, estates and private armed men; the flight of the crowned folk south in the Yongjia disaster became a cultural watershed lasting a thousand years. Third, the settled Xiongnu, Jie, Xianbei, Di and Qiang used the disorder to found their own states: Former Zhao (Han-Zhao) and Cheng-Han were both established in 304, and Later Zhao, Former Yan and Former Qin followed, so that the north entered the age of the Sixteen Kingdoms and nearly three centuries of war followed, with ethnic relations shifting from fusion to violent collision. Fourth, institutional change: the regionalisation of armies and of command became the norm, the theatre commander holding troops and provinces raising their own picked troops was fixed as a pattern, while the nine-rank system and the great clans, pressed by the disorder, grew firmer and became the source of the Sui and Tang examination system. Fifth, Buddhism and steppe culture pushed deeper into the Central Plains amid the chaos: monks such as Fotucheng went north around the fall of Luoyang, Shi Le of Later Zhao treated him with respect, and monasteries and steppe customs entered the northern cities together. Sixth, a change in the very idea of war: for the first time in China cavalry decided the political fate of the Central Plain on a scale that outweighed the infantry, and the principle of defeating foot with horse became the basic military premise of the northern regimes that followed.
result: 結果沒有勝者，只有代價。306年太安二年，六月晉惠帝在洛陽被毒死，七月東海王司馬越病卒於鄴，隨即被追贈為丞相，軍隊與權柄在他死後迅速分崩：其部將與豫州、並州的地方勢力各自擁兵，朝廷無力制止。同一時期劉聰已於永嘉元年稱帝，二年遣劉曜大敗晉軍於洛陽之西，三年再度圍洛，懷帝出奔，311年洛陽終於陷落，懷帝被俘至平陽，長安孤立，愍帝於建興元年（313）即位，四年而國亡。於是北方政權分立，317年司馬睿在建康即位，東晉偏安江左，中原士族「衣冠南渡」，而留居北方的漢人則在十六國諸政權的征調、屠殺與混戰中大量死亡，漢語、漢俗與漢族身份的傳承在地區的分裂中轉為各自保存。八王之中唯一稱帝的趙王司馬倫在位僅約三個月，其餘七人無一善終：亮、瑋被誅，倫自盡，冏被刺，乂被囚而遇害，穎死於劉淵軍中，頴被斬，越病死。從長時段看，這場戰爭的真正受益者是三方：一是趁亂立國的匈奴、羯、氐、羌政權，開啟了北方數百年的族群國家時代；二是南渡並在江南重建秩序的士族集團；三是得以在亂後北伐的祖逖等將領，其部曲一度收復黃河以南，說明亂世之中仍有恢復的可能，而北朝最後的秩序要等到北魏統一北方、孝文帝改革以後才重新建立。
resultEn: The result was no victor, only cost. In the sixth month of Tai'an 2 (306) Emperor Hui of Jin was poisoned to death in Luoyang; in the seventh month Prince Donghai Sima Yue died of illness at Ye and was posthumously honoured as chancellor, and within a short time his command and his armed following fell apart, his generals and the regional powers of Yuzhou and Bingzhou each holding troops of their own while the court could do nothing to stop them. By then Liu Cong had already assumed the imperial title in Yongjia 1, had routed the Jin army west of Luoyang with Liu Yao in Yongjia 2, and had encircled the city again in Yongjia 3; the emperor of Huai fled, and in 311 Luoyang finally fell. The emperor was carried off to Pingyang, Chang'an stood alone, the emperor of Min was enthroned in Jianxing 1 (313), and four years later that state was gone. Northern government therefore broke into many states; in 317 Sima Rui took the throne at Jiankang, the Eastern Jin held only the lower Yangtze, and the great clans of the north, the crowned folk of the Yongjia disaster, moved south, while those Han Chinese who stayed in the north were killed in enormous numbers through conscription, slaughter and the wars of the Sixteen Kingdoms, and the transmission of the language, the customs and the identity of the Han people, cut apart by division, was preserved region by region instead. Of the eight princes only Sima Lun ever took the imperial title, and he held it for roughly three months; the other seven came to no good end. Liang and Wei were executed, Lun took his own life, Jiong was assassinated, Ai was killed in custody, Ying died in Liu Yuan's camp, Yong was beheaded, and Yue died of illness. Seen over the long run, three parties profited from this war: first, the Xiongnu, Jie, Di and Qiang states founded in the disorder, which opened the era of ethnic states in the north for centuries; second, the great clan groups who migrated south and rebuilt an order in the Yangtze delta; and third, commanders such as Zhu Ti, who could still march north after the war and briefly recovered the territory south of the Yellow River, showing that recovery remained possible even in collapse. The last order in the north was not rebuilt until the Northern Wei unified the north and its Xiaowen reforms remade the state.
